title: Signal Harbor — Route & Model Inspector: compact performance probe
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact Route & Model inspector (Signal Harbor) for the Redwood Console focused on per-route and per-model performance metrics. The panel should surface latency percentiles, throughput, token breakdowns (prompt vs generated), and cost attribution so engineers and PMs can triage regressions without leaving the route view. It must support quick variant comparison, short-term time ranges (1m/5m/1h) for incident triage, and include rollout controls (canary toggle, model fallback link). Emphasis on compactness, micro-interactions, and clear affordances for drill-in to full telemetry views.
acceptance_criteria: Compact inspector renders in the route list (collapsed) and expands inline to show detailed charts
Latency chart shows p50/p95/p99 as overlaid sparklines with hover microtraces linking to full traces
Throughput chart supports per-second and per-minute aggregation and displays request count with burst detection highlighting
Token waterfall displays average prompt, generated, and cached token counts and highlights KV-cache hit ratio when available
Cost-attribution line item present per-1k tokens with ability to toggle normalized cost vs absolute cost
A/B rollout affordances: canary percent, toggle to pin variant, and link to rollback/fallback runbook
Figma mockups and prototype clickable on mobile and desktop breakpoints
Design documented with accessible color contrast, alt text for charts, and keyboard navigable tooltip focus
design_notes: Primary UX constraint: render useful triage signals in a 420px wide panel used inline in the Routes table
Charts should favor small-multiples and sparklines instead of full-size time-series to avoid context switching
Latency visualization approach: layered area + median line + percentile bands (p95/p99) using semi-transparent fills for quick visual outliers
Token waterfall: stacked bars with micro-annotations for average token counts and a toggle to show distribution violin on hover
Cost overlay: semi-transparent ribbon on the throughput chart; hover shows cost breakdown by model variant
Interaction: clicking a chart pin opens the full Performance Canvas in a new tab while preserving time-range and filters
Progressive disclosure: show summary values by default; expand to per-variant small-multiples when user clicks 'expand variants'
Mobile: collapse non-critical charts into an accordion; primary metric on top should be latency p95/p99 with an expand affordance
decisions: Use 1-minute aggregation window for default sparklines to balance responsiveness and noise
Latency y-axis will use log scale for mixed short/long tail workloads to preserve readable detail at low ms ranges
Token counts will be normalized to tokens per-request by default; raw tokens available via a toggle
Accessibility: adopt dark+light color swatches from existing Console tokens and verify with Axe and contrast testing
Rollout controls will be read-only unless the user has 'deploy' permissions; permission state exposed by tooltip
tasks: Finalize compact chart specs and annotate axes/units
Prototype interactive sparklines in Figma with hover states
Map data schema required for latency percentiles and token breakdown to backend team
Run accessibility review and adjust colors/contrast
Coordinate with ENG to add canary toggle permission checks
